newsitem.title: USA: HUD gets $1.04 bln return at "large" loan auction.
newsitem.headline: HUD gets $1.04 bln return at "large" loan auction.

text.p: The Department of Housing and Urban Development said Monday it drew a record return of $1.04 billion on its recent "large" sale of troubled mortgages.

The January 28 sale of unpaid loan balances on 18,894 single-family mortgages, conducted by HUD's Federal Housing Administration, yielded the highest return in what was the largest number of loans offered at auction since FHA began the program in 1994.
The sale was the fourth "large" single family sale the FHA has conducted. It drew 1,639 bids from 11 parties. There were three winning bidders and every mortgage was sold.

The competitive auction generated about 92 percent of the mortgages' $1.13 billion total unpaid balances. The FHA said it used a computer optimization model to determine a bid combination that provided the maximum return to taxpayers.

The FHA said that, since the program began, nearly 100,000 troubled mortgages have been sold. The auction is one of a series to sell up to $11 billion in FHA-insured multi-family and single-family mortgages HUD acquired, mostly through default.
